title: "Reading and sources"

## Course baseline

The [official 5MO101 syllabus](https://www.umu.se/en/education/syllabus/5mo101/)
documents the predecessor's scope, modules, outcomes and assessments. Its
reading list is unavailable online. The formal syllabus and literature list
for successor 5MO00S remain unverified here.

## How to use the readings

Each unit provides original explanations and links to relevant public sources.
Read a source with a specific question: what process is being described, what
evidence supports it, and what conditions limit the explanation? The
[literature activity](practicals/literature-presentation.qmd) develops this into
a structured critical reading and presentation.

For prerequisite support, [OpenStax Biology 2e](https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e)
offers an open introductory biology reference. Links within the units point to
more focused sections. Optional R uses the documentation linked from its own
page, rather than requiring a separate computing textbook.

## Candidate specialist references

These are planning references, **not confirmed required purchases**. Assigned
sections and the actual course reading list will be provided later.

- Hill, Cavanaugh and Anderson, *Animal Physiology*, fifth edition.
  [Publisher information](https://www.oup.com.au/books/higher-education/biology/9780197552438).
- Taiz, Møller, Murphy and Zeiger, *Plant Physiology and Development*, seventh
  edition. [Publisher information](https://www.oup.com.au/books/higher-education/biology/9780197577240).

Selected sections can support the topics. The instructor evidence record maps
the proposed units to chapter ranges. Exact adopted editions and section/page
assignments still need the actual literature list.

## Practical materials

The [supplied datasets](downloads.qmd) are simulated and have a design and units
dictionary. They were constructed for these activities, not taken from either
textbook. Tissue identification in the classroom pages prepares students to
describe structure; real-image and specimen recognition still requires the
teaching team's resources. The current materials do not reproduce commercial
textbook figures, laboratory manuals or an official question bank.
